title: The Night Ward
logline: A night-shift nurse on a hospital ward moves from bed to bed in the dark, doing the small physical things, a sip of water, a hand held, for people whose families can't be there.
human_question: What is left to give someone when medicine has done what it can?

premise.story: One overnight shift with a nurse on a general or palliative ward in a provincial hospital, told through her rounds and her own account of the work.
premise.place: A government hospital ward in a Central Province town.
premise.experience: A quiet corridor at 3am, the particular rhythms of a night shift, small physical gestures of care, and a nurse's own, unsentimental words about what she has learned from sitting with many people at the end.

concept_links.why: The source stresses what is done or remembered near the end of a life, and the value of someone nearby who helps a dying person toward something good to hold onto [C056-P:L83; C056-M:L22]. A night nurse's ordinary care sits inside that idea without any doctrine being spoken.

The source describes the dying mind still meeting the world through the senses right up to the end. A nurse's small physical gestures, moistening lips, holding a hand, work at exactly those senses, without the film needing to explain why.

what_must_be_real: The nurse's real work and years of experience. No patient is shown identifiably without explicit, informed consent, and no death is filmed.

possible_arc.opening: The ward settling for the night.
possible_arc.turn: A quiet hour where the nurse talks about what she has seen people return to at the end.
possible_arc.ending_open: Dawn and shift change. The ward keeps going without her.

requirements: A public hospital willing to permit filming under strict patient-privacy conditions
A nurse with long experience willing to speak on camera
No identifiable dying patients shown without consent

suggestions.name: A district or base hospital in the Kandy area
suggestions.why: A public hospital of the right scale for a ward-based observational piece.
suggestions.verify: No specific hospital or ward has agreed to filming; hospital permission and ethics clearance would be required.

drop_if: No hospital grants filming access under safe privacy conditions
The nurse is unwilling to be identified or her patients cannot be adequately protected

connections.note: A companion piece: presence at the very end, seen once in a village home and once on a hospital ward.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
